summary: Scoped obfuscated inference record handoff for cost-scaling root-cause investigation
description:
Issue summary: Billing team detected an unexplained 48-hour spike in per-request spend for a subset of customer traffic. Initial correlation suggests increased token counts for a narrow cohort of requests. We need a timeboxed, scoped extract of inference request/response metadata and obfuscated payload snippets to validate whether prompt shapes or SDK client-side retries are causing the cost escalation.

Impact: Potential customer-facing billing variance and material cost overrun on a Reserved capacity pool. Fast triage needed to determine whether to pause a rollout or apply a conservative cost cap.

Justification: This is a targeted investigation into a measurable billing anomaly. Full raw payload export is not required; we propose an obfuscated, schema-preserving sample to preserve debugging signal while minimizing exposure of customer PII.

Data requested: 1) Request metadata (timestamp, route, model, token_count_in, token_count_out, request_id, customer_org_id hashed) for all requests matching the cohort filter for 2026-03-07 00:00 to 2026-03-08 23:59 UTC. 2) For a sampled 1% of those requests (max 5k records), include obfuscated prompt/response snippets where free-text is replaced with deterministic HMAC-tokenized placeholders and length-preserving masks. 3) KV-cache hit/miss flag and note if reroll/fallback model was used.

Minimization & safeguards: - Timeboxed access window: 72 hours from approval. - Export stored only on an encrypted, ephemeral S3 bucket with account-level KMS key; bucket TTL 7 days then auto-delete. - Analysts will use short-lived IAM role (one-hour session duration) with CloudTrail and object-level logging enabled. - Sensitive fields (user identifiers, email-looking strings, payment-like patterns) will be redacted or replaced with hashing+salting before any human review.

Access list: Billing investigator (Priya Nair), SRE investigator (Alex Rivera), one Privacy reviewer (Jordan Blake). Additional auditors: Legal on-call (TBD).

Desired outcome: Determine whether token inflation is caused by client retry loops, prompt templating changes, or model-side behavior; recommend either throttle rules, client guidance, or model roll-back.

Time sensitivity: High — billing team requests findings within 48 hours to decide next steps for cost controls.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Query prod request catalog using cohort filter: route contains '/v1/generate' AND model = 'redwood-v1-large' AND token_count_in > 500. 2) Narrow to orgs with >1000 requests in the 48-hour window. 3) For sample selection, apply deterministic hash on customer_org_id then select lowest 1% buckets to ensure reproducibility. 4) Run extract job on replica read-only analytics cluster via ad-hoc ETL job (etl/billing/cohort_extract_20260307.sql).
logs: Log sources: s3://redwood-prod-logs/inference/requests/2026/03/07-08/, CloudWatch stream: /prod/serving/runtime, Datadog dashboard: Billing > TokenCost > Spike-2026-03-07 (dash-778). Example request trace id: req_20260307_9f8a3b2c. Query job history: airflow run billing.cohort_extract 2026-03-12T03:00Z (pending approval).
investigation_notes: Initial automated sampling run (non-sensitive metrics only) shows median token_count_in increased from 120 to 820 for the cohort; token_count_out variance also up 3x. No obvious single client version dominates; traffic distribution more skewed to three org IDs (obfuscated hash prefixes: a1b2, c3d4, e5f6). Hypotheses: 1) SDK retry bug sending full prompt multiple times, 2) template change on customer side adding long embeddings, 3) an upstream proxy duplicate-ing requests. SRE recommends small scoped extract to validate. Prior linked ticket INT-903210 contains model routing decision traces that may be useful.
